sentences.text:
The petitioner, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, seek quashing of FIR No. 867/2015 dated 22.04.2015 registered under Sections 498A/406/468/471/465 IPC at P.S Shakarpur, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Memorandum of Understanding dated 14.03.2023 arrived at between the parties.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Memorandum of Understanding dated 14.03.2023 [Annexure-P2] and is also supported by affidavits of the petitioner and of respondent no.2,
alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 8720/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:23:13 3.
Petitioner as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.

5. Learned APP for the State and learned counsel for the respondent no.2 accept notice.
6.
Learned APP for the State has handed over the Status Report which is taken on record.
As per the FSL Report, the story of the prosecution qua forgery has been negated.

1 has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
7.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 12.09.2023.

She further affirms the Memorandum of Understanding dated 14.03.2023 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.18,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.7,00,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no. 2 vide DD no. 905266 issued on State Bank of India, New Delhi, in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

8. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is CRL.M.C. 8720/2023 page 2 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 14/12/2023 at 02:23:13 of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

9. Accordingly, the petition is allowed and FIR No. 867/2015 dated 22.04.2015 registered under Sections 498A/406/468/471/465 IPC at P.S Shakarpur, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom are quashed.

10. Needless to state that the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way, effect the rights of the child of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 namely Ms. Komal vis-a-vis her parents,
as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
11.

The petition alongwith the pending application stands disposed of.
